$comment: OQ-HA-01 assumption. opencode does not enumerate its tool surface headlessly - `opencode debug v2` returns providers and models, not tools - so this snapshot is the oracle instead. Every name in `tools` MUST be classified by .opencode/lib/harness-core.js as write, read-only or unsupported; an unclassified tool blocks at runtime (FR-HA-11), and this file is what makes that block land in CI before it lands on a user. Refresh it on an opencode version bump, deliberately, and classify anything new in the same change.
$how_captured: Union of the resolved `tools` maps reported by `opencode debug agent <name>` across build, plan, general, explore, developer, tech-lead, auditor and qa-engineer. An earlier version of this file was written from the permission-key list in the published docs and listed four tools that no agent actually exposes (list, websearch, lsp, todoread) while missing the real name of the patch tool. A snapshot that is not a capture is not an oracle.

$not_exposed.$comment: Present in the binary but absent from every resolved tool map on this version. Classified anyway, so that enabling one cannot quietly become an unguarded write.
$not_exposed.apply_patch: unsupported - writes files without naming them in its arguments
